title: The dark age is a knife
word: The dark age is a knife
hookLine: this age is a knife, kings are butchers, and righteousness has flown (Majh ki Var, ang 145)
tomorrow: Hard to be called a Muslim

cards: The age is a knife. The kings are butchers. Righteousness has grown wings and flown away.

That's one salok in Guru Nanak's ballad in Majh, in plain English, not word for word. It doesn't sound like a hymn. It sounds like a headline: no soft opening, just three blunt pictures, one after another.
And then, in the next breath, the lights go out.

teach.h: KAL: THE DARK AGE BECOMES A BLADE.
teach.b: The age is Kal, the Kali Yuga, the dark age in the old Indian reckoning of time, and Guru Nanak makes it a blade.
The salok goes on, again in plain English: falsehood is the night of the new moon, and the moon of truth can't be seen rising anywhere. I've searched and searched, and I'm bewildered.
In the darkness there's no path to be seen. People cry out in pain, caught in their own ego. Says Nanak, how will anyone be saved?
Three things to notice. First, he names who holds the knife.

Not demons, not fate: kings, the people trusted with power. The Babarvani hymns, a few days back, said something like it about an invasion; here it widens into a picture of an age. Second, righteousness isn't killed.
It flies. It grows wings and leaves, which means it was able to go, and might be able to return. Third, Nanak puts himself in the dark too.

He doesn't stand above the age pointing down; he stands inside it, looking for the moon. The salok ends on a question, not a slogan, and other lines of the Var answer it with the Guru, the lamp it opened with.
An age can cut. Power can butcher.
Truth can hide like the moon on a dark night. And still someone keeps searching the sky for it.
That's today's line: a knife of an age.

how: This salok is sung and read as part of Majh ki Var in the Guru Granth Sahib, and in katha it is explained as Guru Nanak's plain speech about rulers and the darkness of falsehood.

games.q: what does “the dark age is a knife” mean?
o: Nanak's picture of an age that cuts, where kings butcher
a sword Guru Nanak carried through a dark time
a warning that the world will end in a great war

games.q: what's in the salok — tap the pairs.
p: the night of the new moon

s: in the salok, righteousness is killed by the kings
it grows wings and flies away. it leaves; it isn't destroyed.
Guru Nanak places himself in the dark, searching
he says he has searched and is bewildered; in the darkness he can't see the path.
the salok ends with a tidy answer
it ends on a question: says Nanak, how will anyone be saved?

games.q: the age is a knife, the kings are butchers, and the moon of truth can't be seen. you're Guru Nanak. what does the salok show you doing?
o: searching in the dark, and asking how anyone will be saved.
games.why: he searches, says he's bewildered, and ends with a question. the Var answers it elsewhere with the Guru, the lamp it opened with.

practice: Bring to mind, one at a time, the people who hold power over your life, in your town, your country, your work, and instead of arguing with them in your head, picture the moon of truth rising over each, a small light in a dark sky.
If you pray, ask God in your own way for honesty in those who lead; if you don't, simply wish it for them, and for the people under them.

wordCard.voice: The dark age is a knife. Guru Nanak's salok in Majh ki Var: the age cuts, kings are butchers, righteousness has flown, and truth's moon hides, while he keeps searching. Today's word.

orig.note: kal kati: 'the dark age is a knife', the salok's first words.

carryVoice: Your line: a knife of an age. Nanak's question still stands, and so does his searching. Same time tomorrow.
